mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced equity risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0 in the month before decision
regime_hint: FED Funds rate near or above 4% target zone
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative when FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, with p-value > 0.05 in t-test vs. pre-increase period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market strengthening offsets inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND UNRATE < previous month
regime_hint: Labor market improving while inflation is moderate
failure_condition: In 60-day rolling window, the interaction has Rank IC < 0.05 and no significant positive return over the 20-day horizon when both conditions hold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in GDPC1 (real GDP momentum) of at least 3% followed by a subsequent month of HOUST > 1250 indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with robust consumer spending
failure_condition: Over 12-month period, the signal triggers but 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 100 (vintage) coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing output signals contractionary conditions.
failure_condition: More than 40% of INDPRO < 100 instances do not precede negative 5-day returns (independent t-test, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00 for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as markets anticipate prolonged easing and lower rates.
failure_condition: Over 100 such streaks, no significant positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in UNRATE above 5% in a month when PAYEMS is flat suggests labor market cooling, resulting in a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Labor market cooling with stable employment
failure_condition: In 60-day windows, the interaction does not precede negative 20-day returns with statistically significant effect (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both GDPC1 and INDPRO by at least 2% indicates weakening economic momentum, producing a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Consecutive monthly declines in GDP and industrial output
failure_condition: Over 50 such double declines, no significant negative 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL above 250 (vintage) followed by a 20-day positive S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate inflation acceleration and rate hikes, but only in non-recession regimes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 250 AND not in recession regime
failure_condition: During inflation spikes in non-recession periods, 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline (p > 0.05).
